classification.class: SAX1 start-tag bookkeeping leaves pushTab null and later reads through it

bug_description.original: A bad-cast/UBSan error in parser.c's xmlParseElement causes a null pointer dereference (read from a near-zero address) when handling certain inputs. The invalid cast to an xmlStartTag-like structure leads to a segmentation fault and undefined behavior during parsing, which can be triggered by crafted XML and results in a denial-of-service crash.
bug_description.normalized: The testcase controls parser options and XML bytes so libxml2 enters a SAX1 element-start path where xmlParseElementStart records the open element with namePush instead of nameNsPush. namePush increments ctxt->nameNr and stores ctxt->nameTab but does not allocate or populate ctxt->pushTab. When parsing later hits premature EOF, xmlParseElement assumes the parallel pushTab entry exists and reads ctxt->pushTab[ctxt->nameNr - 1].line, producing the observed near-null read from a null base pointer.

source.value_from: The fuzz testcase supplies both parser options and the main XML entity. Those options can set XML_PARSE_SAX1 through xmlCtxtUseOptions, and the main entity bytes are then consumed here as a SAX1 start tag.
source.description: This is the first project statement on the crashing path that consumes attacker-controlled XML bytes into the vulnerable parser state consistent with the bug: a SAX1 start-tag parse whose result is later recorded with namePush rather than nameNsPush.

sink.description: The premature-EOF path dereferences the missing pushTab entry for the current open element, applying the observed non-zero offset to a null pushTab base.

root_cause.description: In the SAX1 branch, xmlParseElementStart records the open element only with namePush. That increments nameNr and stores the element name but leaves the parallel pushTab metadata array unallocated and uninitialized even though later code unconditionally reads pushTab[nameNr - 1].line.

parser_admitted.description: The crafted main entity is accepted as an element start in the SAX1 parsing branch.

tainted_value_origin.note: The testcase controls parser options, including the XML_PARSE_SAX1 bit that selects the vulnerable namePush branch. The same testcase later provides the main entity bytes through xmlFuzzMainEntity.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness reads attacker-controlled parser options and the main XML entity, then configures a push parser with those options.
A SAX1 start tag is parsed and recorded with namePush, which advances the name stack without creating the matching pushTab metadata entry.
When the same element later reaches premature EOF, xmlParseElement reads pushTab[nameNr - 1].line and crashes because pushTab was never populated for that open element.

fine_trace.note: The testcase's leading bytes are consumed as parser options; these options are later applied to the push parser and can select SAX1 behavior via XML_PARSE_SAX1.
With SAX1 behavior selected, the parser consumes attacker-controlled XML bytes as a start tag and materializes the element name that will be recorded as an open element.
The vulnerable path takes the false branch here, so the parser skips nameNsPush and stays on the SAX1 bookkeeping path.
namePush stores the parsed element name in nameTab and increments nameNr, but unlike nameNsPush it neither allocates pushTab nor writes the line metadata entry for this open element.
The testcase leaves the current element unfinished so parsing reaches the premature-EOF error path that reports the open tag's line number.

Because step 4 advanced nameNr without creating the matching pushTab entry, this read uses a null pushTab base with index nameNr - 1 and triggers the observed near-zero-address access at offset 24, the line field inside xmlStartTag.

sanitizer_ground_truth.trace_format: UBSan runtime error with corroborating ASan crash trace from Stage 01 artifacts
sanitizer_ground_truth.crash_type: null-base field read through missing start-tag metadata entry

poc.trigger: The testcase controls both parser options and the main XML entity so that libxml2 parses at least one SAX1 start tag, records it with namePush, and later reaches xmlParseElement's premature-EOF path for that still-open element.

format.name: libxml2 fuzz-entity container carrying parser options and XML text
format.contract: The witness file is a libxml2 fuzz input, not raw XML alone. It begins with an option word consumed by xmlFuzzReadInt, then provides the main entity through the fuzz string/entity framing used by xmlFuzzReadEntities. The XML text only needs to make libxml2 open an element on the SAX1 path and then hit premature EOF before that element is closed; the saved artifacts do not justify a narrower byte-level contract than that.
